messages:
sam: Quick sync — I'm assembling the final acceptance checklist for the Reserved Pools PRD. Focus: SLA floor, burst behavior, autoscale signals, and rollback triggers.

tara: +1. Can we lock numeric targets today? Need them for the sales deck.

ben: Proposed targets from infra experiments: p95 <= 120ms, p99 <= 300ms for text-generation small models at steady state (1k concurrent tokens/s per pool).

lee: For throughput sizing we used a conservative GPU unit of 10k tokens/s for v1 pools (NVIDIA A10-ish). That maps to ~100 steady active users for our thready workloads.

maria: For SLA floor we should state: 99.5% availability per billing month, and SLOs on latency that are best-effort with credits for p99 violations?

sam: Draft acceptance bullets I want in PRD: 1) SLA metric definitions (availability, error rate), 2) Throughput sizing calc with test harness, 3) Autoscale signals and safe cooldowns, 4) Burst policy & bounded best-effort behavior, 5) Canary + rollback rules, 6) Runbook for degraded modes.

ben: Autoscale signals we measured that worked: sustained queue depth > 200 tokens for 20s, or tail latency trending up > 25% for 30s. Cooldown: 90s min between scale-up events, 10m ramp-down.

lee: Agree on cooldowns. Add a cap: no more than 3 scale-ups in a 10m window to prevent oscillation.

tara: Burst policy ask from BE customers: allow 2x short bursts for up to 60s. After that, fall back to best-effort throttling with graceful 429s or queued responses. We need clear behavioral acceptance criteria for fallback.

sam: Acceptance criteria (concrete): - Under normal load (<= provisioned capacity) p95 <= 120ms and error rate < 0.1% over 24h test. - Under 2x burst for <=60s: 95% of requests either served within 2x latency target or return well-formed 429 with Retry-After header. - Autoscale triggers must bring additional capacity in <120s 90% of the time during realistic ramp tests. - Canary rollout: if service error-rate increases >0.5% or p99 > 2x baseline for 10m, auto-roll back to previous model variant.

maria: We should also define audit logs and cost telemetry acceptance: per-request cost tags and per-pool cost dashboard available in Console.

ben: Edge case: long KV-cache warmup for chat-like flows can blow p99. Add requirement: warmup-probing path that prefetches KV cache for pinned sessions during scale-up. Test case included.

lee: Implementation note: batch sizes will vary. PRD should require runtime to expose average batch size and token amplification metrics so we can validate cost per token.

tara: Who owns end-to-end validation? Suggest product owns test scenarios, eng-runtime owns harness and infra. Need an owner for acceptance sign-off.

sam: I'll own PRD sign-off, ben and lee will own validation harness and test runs, tara will coordinate sales/cust acceptance items. Add infra-bot integration to post canary metrics to #eng-runtime.

infra-bot: scheduled-test: reserved-pools-loadtest v2 queued, expected run start 1715600000. Results will post in thread.

maria: One more: SLA credits calc in PRD must be explicit and tested via chaos scenarios (region failover + pool preemption). Add two chaos playbooks.

sam: Great. Next steps: I will update PRD with these numeric acceptance criteria and push a draft to the repo by EOD. Please drop any must-have test cases here before 16:00.

tara: adding a test case: degraded-network (10% packet loss) with normal token arrival pattern. Want to see graceful fallback.

ben: adding a test case: model-variant-fallback under 30% reduced capacity. Verify routing fallback correctness and no user-facing corrupted outputs.

lee: adding a test case: KV-cache cold start with 5k pinned sessions ramping concurrently.

sam: 👍 thanks everyone. I'll post the PRD link once pushed.

maria: thanks — will prepare compliance checklist for Private deployments after PRD lands.
